topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This section provides introductory framing and outlines the learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Cancer etiology, mutation sources, and epidemiological variation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational drivers of cancer by examining the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how infectious pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, focusing on Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed mechanistic example.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical and cellular processes through which chemical and physical mutagens induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, host susceptibility, and carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic tumor promotion, microenvironmental factors, and host developmental susceptibility in cancer development.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and evaluating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, and experimental methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate their risks.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This section provides the final summary and closing remarks for the lecture.
